parsed.why: Totalitarian regime, undefined morality laws applied at official discretion, no civil society, forced concealment, official hostility, dated defector accounts of execution. Discovery as trans would likely mean detention in a camp system.

No same-sex criminalisation, but no protections, police blackmail of LGBT people, hostile legislators, anti-propaganda law, contracting public life. Outed trans visitor faces police discrimination and social hostility without recourse.

Strong anti-discrimination law and legal recognition, progressive reputation, official condemnation of Pride attacks; offset by documented Pride violence, vague and rarely enforced protections, weak hate-crime framework.

Statutory gender-identity anti-discrimination in force, decriminalised, no documented trans-specific abuse or state hostility, but thin record, no documented social acceptance or trans-visitor-specific protections.

Same-sex conduct and public same-sex contact criminalised, no legal recognition, documented state campaigns of beating/arrest, bathroom arrest; partly offset by health-ministry inclusion policy and active legal-aid organisation.
